questions.explanation: Stative passives use 'be' to describe a state: 'is closed'.
questions.q: The museum ___ closed on Mondays.

questions.explanation: Passive with a modal: 'must + be + past participle'.
questions.q: All applications ___ submitted before the deadline.

questions.explanation: 'Should have been + past participle' criticizes a past omission in the passive.
questions.q: The documents ___ signed by now.

questions.explanation: 'Be interested in' is a stative passive describing a state.
questions.q: I ___ interested in ancient history.

questions.explanation: Modal passive: 'can + be + past participle'.
questions.q: This problem ___ solved easily.

questions.explanation: A completed past action uses 'was built', not the stative 'is built'.
questions.q: The bridge ___ built in 1902 and still stands.

questions.explanation: Modal passives need 'be + past participle': 'must be baked'.
options: The cake must bake for 30 minutes.
The cake must been baked for 30 minutes.
The cake must to be baked for 30 minutes.
The cake must be baked for 30 minutes.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: 'Be opposed to' is a stative passive describing an attitude.
questions.q: She was ___ to the proposal from the start.

questions.explanation: Future passive with a modal: 'will + be + past participle'.
questions.q: The new law ___ be enforced strictly.

questions.explanation: 'Get + past participle' forms a stative-like passive: 'got stuck'.
questions.q: He got ___ in the storm last night.

questions.explanation: Past criticism in the passive: 'should have been announced'.
questions.q: The results ___ announced yesterday.

questions.explanation: 'Was locked' describes the state of the door when they arrived.
questions.q: The door ___ locked, so we couldn't get in.

questions.explanation: Modal passive: 'must + be + past participle'.
options: The work must be finished today.
The work must be finish today.
The work must to be finished today.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: Past passive needs 'was + past participle' and 'by' for the agent.
options: The thief was caught the police.
The thief caught by the police.
The thief was caught by the police.
The thief was catch by the police.
questions.q: Choose the correct sentence.

questions.explanation: Past possibility in the passive: 'could have been completed'.
questions.q: The project ___ completed on time with better planning.

questions.explanation: 'Be delighted' is a stative passive describing a feeling.
questions.q: They were ___ with the service.

questions.explanation: 'Can + be + past participle' expresses passive possibility.
questions.q: The ancient ruins ___ be seen from the hilltop.

questions.explanation: A confident deduction about the past in the passive: 'must have been delivered'.
questions.q: The parcel ___ delivered this morning.

questions.explanation: Past passive needs the past participle 'written', not 'wrote'.
options: The road is closed for repairs.
She is married to a doctor.
questions.q: Find the sentence with a mistake.

questions.explanation: 'May + be + past participle' forms the modal passive.
questions.q: New safety rules ___ be introduced next year.
